source: LiteLLM gateway metrics of the KI cluster (aiaas-prod) in the self-service Prometheus on prod, 2026-11-11 to 2026-11-25 (retention starts 2026-11-11): litellm_input_tokens_metric_total, litellm_output_tokens_metric_total, litellm_proxy_total_requests_metric_total, litellm_in_flight_requests by team_alias and requested_model. The metrics carry no key, user or user agent, so per-person numbers are team numbers divided by the people known to be there; the tool is told from the model alias (code, agent, chat-*). Workspace sizes from aiaas-deployment ansible/templates/jupyterhub-values.yaml.j2 (requests, which is what the AI service books as vCPU and RAM hours). Prices from the token price fix of 25.11.2026 (aiaas-management-api LLM_DOLLARS_PER_MTOKENS 0.5, LiteLLM code/agent 5e-7 input, 1.5e-6 output).

code.source: measured: course Datenanalyse mit R (team ma-t-inf-23iki1-datenanalyse-r, about 20 students with Positron, alias code), 308 successful requests with 3.93 M input and 58 k output tokens = 12.8 k input and 190 output per request; sessions 16.11. and 23.11.2026: 3.63 M and 2.04 M input tokens in the 4 hours, i.e. 182 k and 102 k per enrolled person and 4-hour window (52 k and 29 k per enrolled person-hour), peak 485 k tokens per minute over 2 minutes = 24 k per enrolled person; 86 requests (about 20 %) refused with 429, so the course was throttled and these are lower bounds. typical 10 requests/h ≈ 130 k tokens per person-hour is the course leader's figure (mail 25.11.2026); high 25 requests/h and 50 k TPM are assumptions (factor 2.5 and 2), not measured. concurrent_share (people active in the same minute when they do not work at the same time) is an assumption.

agent.name_en: Agent mode (assistant works on its own)
agent.source: partly measured: alias agent, 19 k input per request in the R course (130 requests), 36 k in a single-person test project (25 requests, 610 k tokens in its busiest hour), 300 output per request; requests per hour and peak TPM are assumptions from the TODO concept (100 k+ per minute of work), not measured per person.

chat.source: mostly assumed: the TODO concept (a few thousand tokens per request, 10 to 20 per hour); the only data, a single-person project on chat-default, had 6 requests with 4.3 k input and 1 k output each. LibreChat's own traffic is not in the metrics by team.

script.source: placeholder: a script's numbers belong to the script; give requests per hour and tokens per request in the request. For comparison, a student app (team StuddyBuddy, alias agent) used 2.6 k input and 340 output per request, at most 170 k tokens in an hour.

key_window.source: aiaas-management-api LLM_KEY_BUDGET_WINDOW (4h) and LLM_KEY_BUDGET_SHARE (0.05): every key may spend that share of its project's 30-day pool per window

pricing.source: the AI service turns llm-mtokens into a LiteLLM money budget at LLM_DOLLARS_PER_MTOKENS = 0.5 per million (reference price 5e-7 per token); LiteLLM bills code and agent 5e-7 per input and 1.5e-6 per output token; chat-large three times chat-default (catalogue text). To be replaced by the documented reference price of the token price fix.

workspaces.source: requests of the JupyterHub profiles (cpu 0.5 cores / 2 GB guaranteed, limit 4 / 8 GB; gpu 1 core / 2 GB and one GPU); the AI service books requested cores and GB × hours. gpu_time_share of CPU + GPU kernel (the GPU is held only while a GPU kernel lives) and concurrent_share are assumptions.

cloud.source: flavours come from OpenStack (public ones for everybody, private ones as granted availabilities of the budget); fallback_flavors only when OpenStack is not connected
